extracted.intended_audience: humor researchers and experimental psychologists studying joke appreciation
extracted.subtask_description: Apply the Ruch 3-WD instrument to classify jokes across three content/style dimensions (incongruity-resolution, nonsense, sexual) and rate each joke's funniness and aversiveness, producing six scores per item. Useful for experimental measurement and for relating joke preferences to personality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funniness rating (f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate each joke/cartoon on how funny it is (funniness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a 1–7 scale. Funniness scores are computed separately for each of the three factors (INC-RESf, NONf, SEXf) depending on the joke's classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aversiveness rating (a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate each joke/cartoon on how aversive it is (aversiveness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a 1–7 scale. Aversiveness scores are computed separately for each of the three factors (INC-RESa, NONa, SEXa) to capture dislike/upset independent from funniness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity-Resolution humor (INC-RES)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes with a clear setup, an incongruous twist, and a resolvable punch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classical joke structure: the audience finds the resolution and experiences satisfaction. Tag items as INC-RES when the incongruity is resolved by the punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonsense humor (NON)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes where the incongruity is NOT fully resolved; absurd or surreal items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes surreal one-liners and anti-jokes where resolution is partial or playful rather than fully resolving the incongruity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual humor (SEX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes whose content involves sex or eroticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sexual content is treated as an independent dimension from the incongruity-vs-nonsense distinction; tag items that rely on sexual/erotic themes as SEX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-scores output (INC-RESf/NONf/SEXf; INC-RESa/NONa/SEXa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every item yields six scores: funniness and aversiveness for each of the three factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and analyze these six scores rather than a single overall funniness; names conventionally used are INC-RESf, NONf, SEXf and INC-RESa, NONa, SEXa.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3-WD style tagging checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Five-step tagging procedure for each joke: 1) Is it incongruity-resolution? 2) Is it nonsense? 3) Is it sexual? 4) What is the funniness score (1–7)? 5) What is the aversiveness score (1–7)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the three binary/nominal content/style tags (INC-RES, NON, SEX) and collect both affective ratings. The checklist operationalizes the instrument for coding materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation: personality correlates and audience-dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Different personality types prefer different humor styles (conservatives → Incongruity-Resolution; open personalities → Nonsense; sensation-seekers → Sexual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use personality measures to predict differential preferences; interpret a joke's quality relative to audience type rather than assuming a single universal funniness ranking. Emphasizes scoring on multiple dimensions instead of a single funniness metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological implication: multidimensional evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Joke quality should be assessed across multiple dimensions rather than by a single funniness score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the same joke can rate high for one personality and low for another, analyses should report dimension-specific funniness and aversiveness and consider audience composition when comparing items.
